## Brand Strategy
- **Purpose:** Inspire human potential every day.
- **Vision:** Build a better world through sport.
- **Positioning:** Unite the world on and off the field of play.
- **Values:** Excellence, Respect, Friendship.
- **Brand characteristics:** Hopeful, Universal, Inclusive, Vibrant, Progressive -- can be "dialled up or down" to reflect different needs.
- **Brand framework:** Purpose > Vision > Positioning > Values -- designed to bring purpose to every expression.
- **Narrative:** "Just like in sport, there are lines to stay within, but those margins aren't meant to stop the exceptional; they simply frame it."

## Logo
- **Olympic symbol (rings):** Five interlocked rings representing five continents (Africa, Americas, Asia, Australia, Europe). Designed by Pierre de Coubertin, debuted 1920.
- **Full colour:** Blue, yellow, black, green, red on white background (preferred version).
- **Monochrome:** Black or white rings on solid colored backgrounds.
- **Construction:** Strict geometric grid; one ring = 12x the thickness of a ring. Space between rings = one ring thickness.
- **Isolation area:** 1/4 ring diameter on all sides. No overlap from any element.
- **Minimum size:** 8mm / 30px wide (exceptions require IOC consent).
- **Logo system:** Two tiers -- Tier 1 (core Olympic logos) and Tier 2 (sub-brands/programs). Multiple colourways documented.
- **Photo placement:** Full-colour rings on light photo backgrounds only (max 5% black tint). Monochrome for other photo backgrounds.
- **Misuse rules:** No unauthorized one-colour versions, no shadows, no color modifications, no rotation, no recreation with objects, no element overlay, no imagery fills, no gradients, no distortion.

## Typography
- **Three exclusive custom typefaces:**
  - **Olympic Headline:** Bold, athletic, uppercase only. Designed 2020 by Julien Hebert (Montreal). Inspired by Tokyo 1964 and Seoul 1988 Olympic typography. Three width variants (Regular, Condensed, Compressed) plus italics. Variable font available. Used sparingly for impact headlines (max 12 words Regular, max 6 words Condensed/Compressed).
  - **Olympic Sans:** Clear, Swiss-inspired workhorse typeface. Contemporary interpretation of Akzidenz-Grotesk (original 1896). Designed 2020 by Fabian Harb (Basel). Regular, Italic, Bold, Bold Italic.
  - **Olympic Serif:** Touch of tradition and elegance.
- **Non-Latin alternates:** Russian (Bebas Neue / Roboto), Chinese (Noto Sans CJK CS), Korean (Noto Sans CJK KR), Japanese (Noto Sans CJK JP), Hindi (Noto Sans Devanagari), Arabic (Noto Sans Arabic).
- **Fallback fonts:** Impact (Headline), Arial (Sans).
- **Detailed specifications:** OpenType features, tracking/kerning/leading, paragraph alignment, rags and widows, line length, typography colour, combining typefaces.

## Color
- **Olympic colours (6):**
  - Blue: Pantone 3005 C / #0078D0 / RAL 5015
  - Yellow: Pantone 137 C / #FFB114 / RAL 1028
  - Black: Pantone 426 C / #000000 / RAL 9005
  - Green: Pantone 355 C / #00A651 / RAL 6037
  - Red: Pantone 192 C / #F0282D / RAL 3020
  - White: Pantone White / #FFFFFF / RAL 9016
- **Medal colours (3):** Gold (Pantone 871 C / #9F8F5E), Silver (Pantone 877 C / #969696), Bronze (Pantone 8023 C / #996B4F). Metallic ink preferred.
- **Extended colours:** Tonal gradations of each Olympic colour for digital interfaces, infographics, illustrations, and product design. Used only in support of Olympic colours, not prominently.
- **Textile specifications:** Cotton TCX and Paper TPX references plus Madeira thread colors.
- **Combining rules:** Olympic and medal colours combine with white or black only. Extended colours only with similar tones.
- **Usage guidance:** "Big hits of white and big hits of colour." Select colours aligned with tone (white = elegant, red = energetic). When in doubt, use white.

## Graphics
- **Graphic devices:**
  - Field of play: Abstract sports field/court shapes used as graphic elements with cropping rules.
  - Sport lines: Geometric line patterns derived from field markings.
  - Combining graphics: Rules for layering devices.
- **Pictograms:** Universal pictogram system. Summer sports (32+), Winter sports, Functional icons. Clear space and minimum size rules. Multiple versions and background treatments. Pictogram colour system. Alignment and grid rules. Container removal options.
- **Illustrations:** Concept-driven illustration system with style/colour guidance, illustration types, combining types, cropping rules, and indexed library.
- **Infographics:** Highlighting data, part-to-whole charts, comparison charts, examples with icons, maps.

## Photography
- **Six categories:** Action, Emotion, Heritage, Editorial, Digital application.
- **Representing diversity:** Explicit requirement for diverse representation.
- **Style guidance:** Post-processing standards, adding elements to photos, treatment rules.

## Applications
- A4 portrait and landscape layouts, display layouts, digital layouts, spacing in digital, layering digital components.
- **Composition:** Grid and format specifications for print and digital. Rings alignment rules. Fine line treatments.
- **Designations and labels:** Naming conventions for Olympic programs and properties.

## Tone of Voice
- Implicit through brand characteristics (Hopeful, Universal, Inclusive, Vibrant, Progressive). The introductory text models the tone: aspirational, inclusive, human-centered. "Let's move the world."

## Outliers
- Three bespoke typefaces each designed by different typographers in different cities (Montreal, Basel) -- connecting Olympic diversity to the type design process itself.
- Olympic Headline deliberately echoes historical Olympic Games typography (1964, 1988) -- brand heritage encoded in letterforms.
- Variable font technology for Olympic Headline (width and slant axes) -- forward-thinking for a brand with deep historical roots.
- Textile-grade color specifications (Cotton TCX, Madeira thread) alongside standard Pantone/CMYK/HEX -- reflecting the vast range of Olympic merchandise and ceremony production.
- Medal colours (Gold, Silver, Bronze) as a formal palette tier is unique to the Olympic brand.
- Extended colour system explicitly restricted from prominent use -- maintaining Olympic colour primacy.
- Field of play graphic devices derived from actual sport playing surfaces -- connecting visual language directly to the sporting experience.
- 129 pages covering the entire visual system including pictograms for all Olympic sports.

## Quality Score
**5 / 5** -- A world-class brand guidelines document befitting the world's most recognized sporting brand. Comprehensive coverage of symbol, colour (with textile/thread specs), three bespoke typefaces with non-Latin alternates, graphic devices, pictograms, illustrations, infographics, photography, and composition grids. The brand framework elegantly connects purpose to visual expression. The system balances deep heritage respect with modern digital and variable font capabilities. Among the most thorough and well-considered brand documents in existence.
